title: Cybersecurity strategy
question: Is there an approved cybersecurity strategy and roadmap, supported by senior management?
remediation: Write a 2-3 year strategy aligned to business goals, get it signed off by leadership and review it yearly.

title: Cybersecurity function and roles
question: Is there a dedicated cybersecurity team or owner, separate from IT operations, with defined roles and responsibilities?
remediation: Appoint a security lead (e.g. CISO), define a RACI for security tasks and keep security reporting separate from IT operations.

title: Security policies
question: Are security policies documented, approved, communicated to staff and reviewed on a schedule?
remediation: Create a policy set (acceptable use, access control, incident response, etc.), get approval, publish it and review at least yearly.

title: Risk management
question: Is there a documented risk assessment method, and are risks assessed periodically and tracked in a risk register?
remediation: Adopt a method (e.g. ISO 27005 style), keep a risk register with owners and treatment plans, and reassess at least yearly or after major changes.

title: Security in IT projects
question: Are security requirements included in IT projects and software development (design review, secure coding, security testing before go-live)?
remediation: Add security checkpoints to the project lifecycle: requirements, design review, code scanning and a pre-release security test.

title: Compliance and audit
question: Are security controls reviewed or audited periodically (internally or by an independent party)?
remediation: Plan a yearly control review, track findings to closure and report results to management.

title: HR security
question: Do staff go through screening, sign confidentiality terms, and have their access removed promptly when they leave?
remediation: Add security clauses to contracts, screen staff in sensitive roles and link HR leaver events to same-day access removal.

title: Awareness and training
question: Is there a regular security awareness programme (including phishing simulations) for all staff?
remediation: Run onboarding and yearly training, plus quarterly phishing simulations; track completion rates.

title: Asset inventory
question: Is there an up-to-date inventory of hardware, software and information assets, each with an owner?
remediation: Build an asset inventory (CMDB or spreadsheet to start), assign owners and classify assets by criticality.

title: Multi-factor authentication
question: Is MFA enforced for remote access, email and all privileged/admin accounts?
remediation: Enforce MFA starting with admins, VPN and email; prefer phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2/authenticator apps over SMS).

title: Least privilege and access reviews
question: Are permissions based on least privilege, with privileged access controlled and access rights reviewed periodically?
remediation: Remove standing admin rights, separate admin accounts, and run quarterly access reviews for critical systems.

title: Endpoint and server protection
question: Do endpoints and servers have anti-malware/EDR, hardening baselines and timely patching?
remediation: Deploy EDR on all endpoints, apply CIS benchmark baselines and set patch timelines (e.g. critical within 14 days).

title: Email protection
question: Is email protected with filtering (spam/malware/phishing) and SPF, DKIM and DMARC?
remediation: Enable advanced email filtering and publish SPF, DKIM and a DMARC policy, moving towards p=reject.

title: Network security
question: Is the network segmented (e.g. user, server, management zones), with firewall rules reviewed regularly?
remediation: Segment networks by trust level, default-deny between zones and review firewall rules every 6 months.

title: Mobile devices
question: Are mobile and BYOD devices managed (MDM), with encryption and remote wipe for devices holding company data?
remediation: Enrol devices in MDM, require screen lock and encryption, and enable remote wipe.

title: Data classification and protection
question: Is data classified (e.g. public/internal/confidential) and protected according to its class?
remediation: Define a classification scheme, label key data stores and apply handling rules (access, sharing, DLP) per class.

title: Cryptography
question: Is sensitive data encrypted in transit and at rest, with a key management process?
remediation: Enforce TLS 1.2+, encrypt disks and databases holding sensitive data, and document key generation, storage and rotation.

title: Backup and recovery
question: Are critical systems backed up, with an offline/immutable copy and regular restore tests?
remediation: Follow 3-2-1 backups with one offline/immutable copy and test restores at least quarterly.

title: Vulnerability management
question: Are systems scanned for vulnerabilities regularly, with remediation timelines based on severity?
remediation: Scan at least monthly, prioritise by CVSS, exploitability and asset criticality, and track fixes against SLAs.

title: Penetration testing
question: Are internet-facing and critical systems penetration tested periodically?
remediation: Commission a pen test of external and critical systems at least yearly and after major changes; retest fixes.

title: Logging and monitoring
question: Are security logs collected centrally (e.g. SIEM), kept for a defined period and monitored for alerts?
remediation: Forward logs from critical systems to a SIEM, define retention, and build alert use cases with someone responsible for triage.

title: Incident response
question: Is there a tested incident response plan, including who must be notified (regulators, customers) and by when?
remediation: Write an IR plan with roles and playbooks, run a tabletop exercise yearly, and document regulator reporting duties (NIS2: early warning within 24h, notification within 72h).

title: Physical security
question: Are offices and server rooms protected with access control and visitor management?
remediation: Restrict server room access with badges/logs, escort visitors and review physical access lists.

title: Web application security
question: Are web applications protected (WAF, secure configuration) and tested against common attacks (e.g. OWASP Top 10)?
remediation: Put a WAF in front of public apps, enforce HTTPS and security headers, and test against the OWASP Top 10 before release.

title: Business continuity
question: Does the business continuity / disaster recovery plan cover cyber incidents (e.g. ransomware) and is it tested?
remediation: Add cyber scenarios to BCP/DR, define recovery time objectives and test the plan yearly.

title: Third-party security
question: Are suppliers assessed for security risk, with security requirements in contracts?
remediation: Tier suppliers by risk, send security questionnaires to critical ones and add security and breach-notification clauses to contracts.

title: Cloud security
question: Are cloud services configured securely and do they meet data hosting/location requirements?
remediation: Review cloud configs against CIS benchmarks, enable cloud logging and confirm data residency rules are met.
